## data

```{r}
set.seed(454)
# load libraries
library(tidyverse) #ofc
library(rstan)
library(readr)
library(bayesplot)
curling <- read_csv("curling.csv") ## make sure to set working directory to source file location
```
```{r message=FALSE}
## to get prior information

canada_ends <- read_csv("Ends.csv") %>%
   filter(TeamID == 10)
canada_games <- read_csv("Games.csv") %>%
  filter(TeamID1 == 10 | TeamID2 == 10)

canada_data <- canada_ends %>%
  left_join(canada_games) %>%
  select(Result, PowerPlay, Winner, TeamID1, TeamID2, CompetitionID) %>%
  mutate(PowerPlay = replace_na(PowerPlay, 0), 
         PowerPlay = ifelse(PowerPlay==0, 0, 1)) %>%
  mutate(CanadaWin = (Winner==0&TeamID1==10)|(Winner==1&TeamID2==10)) %>%
  mutate(j = case_when(CompetitionID == 0 ~ 1, 
                       CompetitionID == 22230015 ~ 2,
                       CompetitionID == 23240026 ~ 3,
                       CompetitionID == 24250026 ~ 4))
```

```{r}
## priors for complete pooling
canada_logitreg <- glm(CanadaWin ~ PowerPlay + Result, data = canada_data, family = "binomial")
complete_priors <- coef(summary(canada_logitreg))
complete_priors
```

```{r}
## get priors for partial pooling 
canada_partial <- data.frame(beta0 = rep(NA, 4), beta1=rep(NA, 4), beta2=rep(NA, 4), se0 = rep(NA, 4), se1=rep(NA, 4), se2=rep(NA, 4))

### step 1: logistic regression for each competition
for(i in 1:4){
  canada_data_competition <- canada_data %>%
    filter(j == i)
  
  model <- glm(CanadaWin ~ PowerPlay + Result, data = canada_data_competition, family = "binomial")
  
  # fill in coefficient estimates
  canada_partial$beta0[i] <- model$coefficients["(Intercept)"]
  canada_partial$beta1[i] <- model$coefficients["PowerPlay"]
  canada_partial$beta2[i] <- model$coefficients["Result"]
  
  # fill in SEs
  canada_partial$se0[i] <- summary(model)$coef["(Intercept)", "Std. Error"]
  canada_partial$se1[i] <- summary(model)$coef["PowerPlay", "Std. Error"]
  canada_partial$se2[i] <- summary(model)$coef["Result", "Std. Error"]
}

## step 2: find means and SDs of the coefficient estimates
### beta0
u0 <- mean(canada_partial$beta0)
v0 <- sd(canada_partial$beta0)
### beta1
u1 <- mean(canada_partial$beta1)
v1 <- sd(canada_partial$beta1)
### beta2
u2 <- mean(canada_partial$beta2)
v2 <- sd(canada_partial$beta2)

## step 3: alpha and beta for the variances
eta0 = mean(1/canada_partial$se0^2) / var(1/canada_partial$se0^2)
alpha0 = eta0 * mean(1/canada_partial$se0^2)

eta1 = mean(1/canada_partial$se1^2) / var(1/canada_partial$se1^2)
alpha1 = eta1 * mean(canada_partial$se1)

eta2 = mean(1/canada_partial$se2^2) / var(1/canada_partial$se2^2)
alpha2 = eta2 * mean(1/canada_partial$se2^2)

```


## models

```{r}
## Complete Pooling approach

# Make data object
run_data <- list(N = nrow(curling),
                 x = as.integer(curling$PowerPlay),
                 y = curling$USWin,
                 z = curling$Points, 
                 m0 = -0.4593229,
                 m1 = 0.8555314,
                 m2 = -0.2783732,
                 s0 = 0.1525552^2,
                 s1 = 0.4249329^2,
                 s2 = 0.1049008^2)

# Fit model in Stan
fit <- stan(file = "completepooling.stan", ## make sure to set working directory to source file location
            data = run_data, 
            chains = 4, 
            warmup = 1000,
            iter = 2000)


```

```{r}
print(fit, pars = c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2"))
plot(fit, pars = c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2"))
traceplot(fit, pars = c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2"), inc_warmup = TRUE)
```
```{r}
## Partial Pooling approach
curling$competition <- as.integer(as.factor(curling$CompetitionName))

# Make data object
run_data <- list(
  N = nrow(curling),
  n_competitions = max(curling$competition),
  j = as.integer(curling$competition),   
  x = as.numeric(curling$PowerPlay),  
  z = as.numeric(curling$Points),       
  y = as.integer(curling$USWin),         
  u0 = u0,
  u1 = u1,
  u2 = u2,
  v0 = v0,
  v1 = v1,
  v2 = v2,
  alpha0 = alpha0,
  alpha1 = alpha1,
  alpha2 = alpha2,
  eta0 = eta0,
  eta1 = eta1,
  eta2 = eta2
)

# Fit model in Stan
partial_fit <- stan(file = "partialpooling2.stan", ## make sure to set working directory to source file location
            data = run_data, 
            chains = 4, 
            warmup = 1000,
            iter = 2000)
```

```{r}
print(partial_fit, pars = c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2"))
plot(partial_fit, pars = c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2"))
traceplot(partial_fit, pars = c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2"), inc_warmup = TRUE)
```
